sanskrit_shloka:
अष्टावक्र उवाच ॥
भावाभावविकारश्च स्वभावादिति निश्चयी ।
निर्विकारो गतक्लेशः सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति ॥ ११-१॥
translation: Aṣṭāvakra said: One certain that the changes of being and non-being arise simply from the nature of things remains unchanging, free from affliction, and easily comes to peace.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Aṣṭāvakra said: One certain that the changes of being and non-being arise simply from the nature of things remains unchanging, free from affliction, and easily comes to peace.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the primary cause of suffering according to Chapter 11?
commentary_faqs.answer: Ashtavakra asserts that suffering arises solely from worry. By realizing that all events are governed by nature or fate, one eliminates worry and attains peace.

commentary_faqs.question: How does this chapter define the relationship between the Self and the body?
commentary_faqs.answer: It teaches the conviction that 'I am not the body, and the body is not mine.' The true Self is pure consciousness, separate from physical attributes and past actions.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the result of realizing that the Lord is the creator of everything?
commentary_faqs.answer: One who is certain that the Lord is the sole creator becomes free from all desires, remains peaceful, and does not attach to any worldly objects or outcomes.

sanskrit_shloka:
ईश्वरः सर्वनिर्माता नेहान्य इति निश्चयी ।
अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः शान्तः क्वापि न सज्जते ॥ ११-२॥
translation: One certain that the Lord, Īśvara, is the maker of all and that here there is nothing else, with all hopes dissolved within, remains peaceful and attaches to nothing.

sanskrit_shloka:
आपदः सम्पदः काले दैवादेवेति निश्चयी ।
तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं न वाञ्छति न शोचति ॥ ११-३॥
translation: One who is certain that adversity and prosperity arise in time by destiny alone remains ever content, with steady senses, neither desiring nor grieving.

sanskrit_shloka:
सुखदुःखे जन्ममृत्यू दैवादेवेति निश्चयी ।
साध्यादर्शी निरायासः कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥ ११-४॥
translation: One who is certain that pleasure and pain, birth and death, are due to destiny alone remains effortless, beholding the inevitable; though acting, one is not tainted by attachment.

sanskrit_shloka:
चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी ।
तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥ ११-५॥
translation: One who is certain that suffering arises from worry, and from no other cause here, becomes free of it and remains happy, peaceful, with longing dissolved everywhere.

sanskrit_shloka:
नाहं देहो न मे देहो बोधोऽहमिति निश्चयी ।
कैवल्यमिव सम्प्राप्तो न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥ ११-६॥
translation: One who is certain, “I am not the body, nor is the body mine; I am pure Consciousness,” lives as though having attained kaivalya, and no longer recalls what was done or left undone.

sanskrit_shloka:
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तमहमेवेति निश्चयी ।
निर्विकल्पः शुचिः शान्तः प्राप्ताप्राप्तविनिर्वृतः ॥ ११-७॥
translation: One who is certain, “From Brahmā down to the smallest blade, all this is myself alone,” remains free of dual conception, pure, peaceful, released from attainment and non-attainment.

sanskrit_shloka:
नानाश्चर्यमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चयी ।
निर्वासनः स्फूर्तिमात्रो न किञ्चिदिव शाम्यति ॥ ११-८॥
translation: One who is certain, “This universe is manifold wonder, yet in truth it is nothing,” becomes free of vāsanās, mere radiance of Consciousness, and rests in peace as though nothing exists.
